subject.title: feat: add opt-in telemetry for native chat lifecycle

question: After current-head runtime proof is refreshed, should the Windows tray adopt this six-span, six-counter, seven-histogram chat telemetry contract with gateway trace propagation deferred?
rationale: The implementation may be technically sound, but its signal names, lifecycle meanings, cardinality bounds, and large tracker become long-lived operator and maintenance commitments requiring product ownership.

options.title: Adopt after fresh proof
options.body: Require redacted 4203fb72 collector evidence, then land the bounded tray-side contract while tracking gateway correlation separately.

options.title: Narrow the initial contract
options.body: Keep only the turn and core send, wait, and receive signals while deferring history, backfill, and dropped-correlation metrics.

options.title: Defer for end-to-end design
options.body: Pause the feature until tray and gateway telemetry can share coordinated W3C context and signal semantics.

recommendation.title: Adopt after fresh proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted 4203fb72 collector evidence, then land the bounded tray-side contract while tracking gateway correlation separately.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest available routing candidate for native tray/chat product direction and long-term operator-facing contract ownership.
